questions.question: Which temperature scale must be used in the ideal gas law?
choices: A scale starting at water's freezing point

questions.question: What does Boyle's law relate for a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature?
What does Charles's law relate at constant pressure and fixed gas amount?
What does the symbol n represent in PV = nRT?
What mainly produces gas pressure on a container wall?
choices: The particles becoming liquid at the wall
Collisions of gas particles with the wall

questions.question: What does Avogadro's law predict at fixed temperature and pressure?
choices: Volume is inversely proportional to the number of moles
Volume is proportional to the number of moles
Every gas has the same particle mass

questions.question: What is a gas's partial pressure?
choices: Half of a gas's total pressure by definition
The pressure only after the gas condenses
The pressure contribution from that gas in a mixture

questions.question: Why does heating gas in a rigid sealed container generally increase its pressure?
choices: Particles collide with the walls more energetically
Heating necessarily adds particles to the sealed container
Particle collisions stop at higher temperature

questions.question: Why does compressing a gas at constant temperature increase pressure?
choices: The sample gains particles without any added gas
Particles strike a smaller available volume's walls more frequently
Particle speed must double despite constant temperature
Pressure falls because the walls are closer together

questions.question: When is an ideal-gas model generally most accurate?
choices: Near condensation at very high pressure
Only when the gas has become a solid
At relatively low pressure and high temperature

questions.question: Why must Celsius readings be converted before using temperature ratios in gas laws?
choices: Gas-law ratios require a zero set at water's freezing point
The kelvin interval is much larger than the Celsius interval
Celsius zero is not absolute zero

questions.question: What happens to gas volume when kelvin temperature doubles at constant pressure and gas amount?
A sealed gas sample expands at constant temperature. What happens to its pressure?
Why does adding gas to a rigid container at constant temperature increase pressure?
choices: Adding particles lowers the collision frequency
Added gas must increase the container's volume
More particles produce more wall collisions
Adding gas lowers pressure by distributing the same particles

questions.question: How is total pressure found for an ideal, nonreacting gas mixture?
choices: Use only the largest partial pressure
Divide by the number of gas species

questions.question: A gas occupies 4 L at 100 kPa. At constant temperature and gas amount, what is its pressure at 2 L?
A gas occupies 3 L at 300 K. At fixed pressure and gas amount, what volume will it occupy at 400 K?
Two nonreacting gases exert partial pressures of 30 kPa and 70 kPa in one container. What is the total pressure?
A rigid sealed container has gas at 200 kPa and 300 K. What pressure does the ideal-gas model predict at 450 K?
Two ideal gases occupy equal volumes at the same pressure and temperature. Which quantities must be equal?
